line: The universe is governed by a law of duality, of opposing forces, everywhere and in everything: opposite the light is dark. They don't cancel each other out but balance each other out, within us and our lives too
We have a drive, a power that wants to carry us towards our dreams and who we're supposed to be. Opposite that good inside you is an opposing force, resistance, as it's called here
Not other people, not anything in your physical world: it lives inside you, living and breathing every day as much as you are

Its one purpose is to push back: to hold you back from where you want to go and who you want to be, to make you stop instead of putting in the effort, to keep you quiet when you should speak up in a relationship
It will be with you every day, in every aspect of your life. You cannot kill it: resistance never dies

Resistance seems to show up in every single aspect of life, so beating it is not about those individual aspects but about stepping back and changing, evaluating and strengthening who you are as a man from the inside out
Get stronger in all the ways resistance can't handle, so you face it every day from strength, as "this big, confident, badass", and it comes cowering

You probably have areas, as is personally the case too, where you're "really kicking his ass", and others where it hands you yours. The more areas you beat it in, the more it gets the message, and the easier it gets
The podcast is about one thing: unleashing your true power by strengthening the man you are, so you battle resistance everywhere from strength
Beating resistance seems to come down to a few things

Physical well-being is absolutely critical: your body affects your mind, emotions, relationships and success in business. You can't attack resistance from your greatest strength without taking care of it, and that starts with fitness, nutrition, the right supplements and optimizing your hormones. When resistance beats you physically, it's like the first battle of the day is already lost, and you go into every other one weaker

Hormones are super important. As they say, "hormones affect everything and everything affects your hormones", and it's so true: how you feel, perceive, act and think, your confidence, your mental and physical well-being. Optimizing them and your testosterone puts you in the strongest position to beat resistance and get what you desire
Fasting is such a powerful tool against resistance, like turning on a "temporary superpower against resistance"

Sexual energy, or sex power, is not just critical in your sex life: it affects your life force energy, drive, confidence, physical energy, joy and happiness, every part of you. Built over time, it carries you to incredible places. Single, married or divorced, there are always ways to harness it, or you can waste it, which drains you physically, of life force energy and against resistance. At the fundamental level it seems to impact literally how strong you are against resistance: the more you build it, the stronger you are, so managing it is amazingly important

The mind. However strong your body and sexual power, if you don't understand your mind and aren't willing to work with it positively, none of the rest matters. It doesn't take a lot: attitude and mindset, working out in a way that builds the mind's strength for tough situations, and a willingness to sit still and meditate for a few minutes
None of this is honestly complicated, but that doesn't mean it's easy. Get after each area every day
Stop comparing your body, business or relationships to anybody else's. Focus on being better today than yesterday, personally the whole aim
We're not wolves, we're human beings. Being an alpha male is not about dominating other people but about dominating resistance within you

The 80/20 principle basically means that 80% of the benefit or results come from 20% of the activity, in everything from personal life to business to milk production in Wisconsin. The book *80/20 Sales and Marketing* by Perry Marshall teaches a lot more about it

For testosterone, the 20% that gives 80%, the "most bang for your hormonal buck", is four areas with three keys each, in no particular order, since where you get the most depends on your particular circumstance
Lifestyle, three keys: sleep, low stress and removing toxins. See [[sleep]], [[stress]], [[toxins]]

For testosterone, sleep is absolutely crucial. Most hormone production happens during sleep, and too little sleep raises cortisol and stress hormones, which really don't coexist with testosterone: more stress hormones generally means lower testosterone. Enough sleep gives double the benefit, too little hurts both ways
Keep stress down, since high cortisol impacts testosterone. Sleep, meditation, exercise and a few supplements help. Personally, the favorite is ashwagandha

For testosterone, remove toxins. The most impactful one you're probably being impacted by is fragrance, in body wash, soap, shampoo, deodorant, cologne, anything listing it: it's highly, highly estrogenic. Keep away from plastic and its chemicals too. There are other areas, but keeping fragrance and plastic out of your life as much as possible gives the most bang for your buck

Nutrition: magnesium matters, with pumpkin seeds a great source, and cruciferous vegetables like broccoli and cabbage remove excess estrogens, but it seems to boil down to three keys: good fats, no toxic fats, no sugar. See [[fats-sugar]]

For testosterone, enough good fats, saturated and monounsaturated, from clean sources: coconut oil, olive oil, organic and sustainably produced palm oil, pasture-raised butter, ghee. They're incredibly important for your brain, and what your body produces hormones from. One big mistake a lot of people make is avoiding fat, and so not getting enough good fats. Of the healthy nuts, macadamia nuts and pumpkin seeds are, personally, two of the only ones really liked, for their fat profile and some other things

Avoid toxic fats "like the plague": basically the polyunsaturated fats, very unstable, which can very easily and will harm your body and hormones. Fried and fast food are absolutely chock full of them, as are a lot of processed and packaged foods. Peanut, canola, vegetable and sunflower oil, among a lot of these oils, are a really potent source

Sugar is absolutely huge, with a direct, significant negative impact on testosterone. In one study, men given sugary syrup saw their testosterone drop 25% and stay lower for hours after. Daily sugar is absolutely going to impact your hormones, and already does every time you consume meaningful amounts. Avoid it like the plague
Sex absolutely impacts your testosterone and hormones in major ways. Three keys: less ejaculation, rarely if ever alone, an active sex life. See [[semen-retention]]
Avoid excess ejaculation: too often, no matter how, it drains your hormones, your life energy, your "qi, as some people call it", in major ways
Stop ejaculating alone, which has the worst impact on your hormones: avoid it ever if at all possible, or do it very, very infrequently

Be active and fuel your sexual energy, with one partner, yourself or multiple partners. It doesn't mean not having sex. Far enough along, it means separating orgasm and ejaculation, so you can be highly sexually active (in general, not with multiple people, though that's your choice). You can absolutely work towards it, and the more you conserve semen, the more you feel it in your hormones, life force energy and mind. The encouragement: learn to ride the edge of not ejaculating while getting the benefits of sexual activity, and eventually to separate ejaculation and orgasm
Fitness, three keys: daily activity, intensity and compound resistance work. See [[intensity]], [[strength]]

Daily activity: you've got to move every day. Hormones are your body's response to its environment: run into a bear on a trail and it spikes adrenaline and cortisol, both hormones. That's largely what hormones really are, in a lot of ways your body's signal and response mechanism. Just sitting signals that you don't really need testosterone. Daily activity signals that you need to be strong and active, so you need testosterone and not too much estrogen

Intensity probably makes a bigger difference in your hormonal response than anything else, and you can feel it. Rather than an hour or an hour and a half of slow, low cardio, you'd be much better off going really hard for 15 minutes, like sprints with short breaks if you want to run. **Story:** going back and forth between climbing and push-ups, really hard, really fast. The harder you go in a short time, the more hormonal benefit

For testosterone, resistance: you've got to get some weight, which doesn't mean lifting heavy all the time, every day, for hours. A couple of sets of some reps with the right activity can have amazing benefits. Use compound exercises with most of your body, especially your lower body: squats, a clean (like a clean and jerk), kettlebell swings, the kettlebell snatch. Whole body, some explosiveness and some weight give the most bang for your buck
Each area holds a lot more detail, and where you get the very most bang for your buck may depend on your specific circumstances

Any fundamental change seems to start with every single day. You are what you do daily, not three times a week, not for two weeks and then stop. What you do every single day for weeks and months literally becomes who you are, not the special events
So to change, improve, add or even subtract something, it's got to be every day. Any attempt to get in shape, eat better or improve a relationship not focused on every day seems destined to fail
Conversely, what you do every single day, not twice a week or twice a month, compounds really powerfully. That's how tremendous changes happen

It works against you as much as for you. **Story:** early in adulthood, absolutely miserable, the daily eating was something like a 7-Eleven hot dog with chili for breakfast and fast food for lunch and on the way home. For a while, almost nightly, literally every single day, came McDonald's and a Taco Bell caramel apple empanada, "this frozen taco thing from hell", with ice cream and caramel syrup added. No Taco Bell in many years now, thank goodness. The result: a disaster zone, physically and mentally
For the most part we seem to want to add things: habits, routines, powers, skills, knowledge, experiences. So it seems fundamental to look at what you do every single day

The podcast is daily for a couple of reasons: to help you feel better and more powerful every day, not occasionally, since every day becomes who you are and the life you experience; and personally, to dramatically impact your life and as many other lives as possible, what is done every single day has to shift

Whatever you want to change, start with every single day, and don't make it negotiable. To get in shape, work out every single day: not the same thing, not crushing yourself nonstop, some days active recovery or whatever. Not three times a week, not a plan, but: "this hasn't been a part of every single day who I am. But going forward, it's gonna be a part of every single day who I am"

Made every day, it becomes who you are instead of something that you do, from working out, eating and your relationship to being a father, your kids, your business, your health. Personally, nothing in life is more important than being a father. Communicating with your spouse, or caring for your body, goes from a few times a week to part of who you are
That's when the really powerful changes happen: you look back and see how dramatically different that part of life used to be. From experience, personally, what leads there is every day

Not "hey honey, we should sit down once a week and talk", not three workouts this week, not attention to your kids two days this week because stress lets you focus only on those two. Not three, two or five times a week. Make it every day, non-negotiable, and you will see tremendous change and impact

Cold is amazing and beneficial on so many levels. There's a lot of science on exposing your body to cold and getting used to it, including incredible immune responses, but personally, the biggest thing found is that it takes you to a deeper, central, more powerful place

Cold is one of the most powerful ways to "kick resistance in the nuts". Society raised us used to being warm and comfortable, and getting uncomfortable through cold has unbelievable benefits against resistance

The encouragement: start one practice, cold showers. **Story:** after cold showers came ice baths, and generally a tank top all winter, seeking the cold whenever possible. There are lots of ways to do it
It's got to be every day: twice a week just doesn't do the same thing. Stick with it a little and, with absolute certainty, you'll feel really amazing benefits
How to take cold showers
The earlier in the day, the better
If you have never taken a cold shower at all, you can start by finishing on cold, then move to just cold

Otherwise, straight cold, maybe with a little warm water to wash, and practice it as much as you can. You can do it a lot more than you think: it takes intentionality and a decision. Gradually build how long you stay in
Benefits of cold showers

Lower stress. The cold stresses your body a little in the moment and, as with lifting weights, body and mind adapt and grow stronger, a huge part being your mind's ability to stay in the moment and not be swept away or crushed by stress

Alertness, not just for the 30 seconds or five or 10 minutes in there but all day. There's really a lot of evidence now, from science and from countless people incorporating cold. It also stimulates deeper breaths, which alone has a lasting effect
Immune response: there are actually studies that found cold showers increase your white blood cells, essentially your body's immune system
The biggest: you literally increase your willpower, your strength against resistance in every area of life
**Story:** strictly cold showers for between two and three years now. Warm showers used to feel good temporarily, then leave a drained and tired feeling

Things that feel good temporarily but leave you worse off suck, like alcohol. Personally, and probably for a lot of people, if you really feel into it, a long, hot shower is that: it feels good, then a lot of times leaves you more drained
Starting your day in a cold shower immediately kicks resistance right in the nuts: not for comfort, but as an intentional choice, for the benefits, strength and internal power it brings
If you've never taken one, it's hard to see cold as anything but discomfort. It is a little, but like working out, it's temporary discomfort that leads to much more powerful things

If you're doing nothing with cold yet, you don't need ice baths or outside cold exposure: please just try a cold shower. They "seriously kick ass" and will change your life. **Story:** after the shift to cold showers, there was never any going back, in years, for the difference they made in life and in the mind
The cold is absolutely your warm friend: inside, where your internal fire, power, willpower and the real you are, is fueled and supported by the cold
We all want to be stronger: it feels good and, especially as men, it brings a different energy to life
Personally, one of the very favorite ways, amazing in how well it works for building strength quickly, is focusing on total daily volume of activity, especially of a couple of simple activities
With push-ups, personally one of the very favorite things to do
Pick a set that pushes you a little but is pretty reasonable, one you can basically do every time, not your absolute max: say 10, if you'd max out at 15, 20 or 25
Do 20, 30, 40 or 50 sets of 10 through the day, starting in the morning, every 15 or 30 minutes, however you want, a set of 10 or two
The longer the period, the better, from waking to bedtime if you can. It doesn't necessarily have to be every 15 minutes

Each set activates those muscles and seems to give them a little signal to grow. A full workout of half an hour to two hours needs at least until the next day to recover. Mini sets aren't intense and don't really break you down: they just say "keep growing", and your body kind of heals a little and grows a little. At least that's the way it seems to work, experientially

If you've never tried it, try it for a week, or three days, even one or two. If you can do five push-ups in a set, aim for at least a hundred for the day, 20 sets of five as a minimum: over five hours, that's a set every 15 minutes, with a timer
Total volume builds really quickly this way, and you'll probably surprise yourself with how much you can do and how fast strength grows

Other exercises: bodyweight or Hindu squats, really excellent for the lower body (if you've never heard of Hindu squats, they work really well for this), or pull-ups, if you can do a set of at least one or two or three. You can mix it up

Pick something you can just get down and do. Squats or push-ups are personally favored because they work anywhere: 10 push-ups take maybe 20 seconds, in the lunchroom at work or at home. After work, 5 to 10 p.m. works too, if you're really diligent with a timer every 15 minutes
If you've never tried it, you'll be amazed how quickly you get stronger. It also seems an awesome way to set a new sort of record for yourself, and it adjusts your perspective

**Story:** never having really done this, or that many push-ups, the goal was a thousand push-ups a day for probably about a week, not reached every day. Surely some guys can do way more, and probably a lot of people can't do one, so the number doesn't matter. What mattered was that a thousand in one workout seemed completely unreachable, yet broken into little chunks through the day, it adds up powerfully
Every day has 96 15-minute increments. Use even half or a quarter of them for one set of something each, and it's amazing how quickly you get stronger
Push-ups are such a basic, functional strength thing that everybody seems able to benefit from more of them, whatever your sport or however you want to improve your body or fitness

The bottom line: lots of sets through the day, targeting a big total daily volume number, 20 to 50 sets of whatever number you can do, varying the hours and the minutes in between. Make each set hard enough to kind of push you while you can still do it every time. By the 40th or 50th set, if you do that many, they obviously get harder. You'll probably be amazed at the results

If it's early enough in the day, try it today: there's such power in today, so don't let it be a tomorrow thing. Even late, kick it off today, then try it tomorrow. It costs one day of effort, and in reality you'll lose nothing and gain a ton. Push-ups, pull-ups and squats all work great, and the recommendation is push-ups, with a high number for the day

If you really dread Monday because you're not digging your work, do something about it: it sucks the life and years out of you. You can't necessarily quit tomorrow, but don't live that way, you don't have to. **Story:** lived that way for a while. "You are not a tree, my friend": you can grow, change and do whatever the hell you want, not stuck in your job, career or situation. If you want to change it, change it

Sex power and sex energy is life force creation energy, the most powerful force we have access to, and the difference between truly harnessing it and wasting it, having it suck life out of you, is almost indescribable. You can harness it in majorly positive ways, single, dating, married or in a relationship

In this view, building sex power the Holistic Alpha way has a few basic, core fundamentals, starting with a couple of things to avoid: porn and jerking off to the point of ejaculation. See [[_parked-sex-energy#Porn]], [[semen-retention]]

Porn fries your brain, your dopamine and so many aspects of your sexuality. It's not the first you've heard of it: there's plenty of science around this now. If it's in your life, it's got to go. Kind of like sugar or alcohol or anything else, the more you take, the greater the negative impact
Like porn, jerking off to the point of ejaculation has to go. The difference between cutting it out and allowing it is absolutely ginormous

Cutting out ejaculating alone doesn't mean not masturbating or exploring your sexuality alone, which is highly encouraged: especially if you're single, to stoke your own fire, and probably in a relationship too, since positive practice makes you better with a partner, in performance, sexual energy and sexual health. But you don't ejaculate

Edging, as a lot of people refer to it: on an arousal scale of 1 to 10, where 10 is ejaculating, you spend time alone without reaching 10, maybe nine or nine and a half, eight or seven, harnessing the energy, feeling the pleasure and fueling your internal fire. An edging session builds your power, even if you're single

The moment you ejaculate, alone or with a woman, you basically hit the reset button: your sexual energy goes back to sort of your baseline, as if nothing had been built. That varies a little with your hormones and situation, but you're back at essentially square one. Ejaculating too often, especially alone, takes you well below it and starts to suck life out of you

Building sexual energy is unbelievably powerful for how you feel physically and mentally, your hormones, your drive and your performance. If you haven't been building it at all, trust that it will have a powerful impact. The Holistic Alpha way, it seems, single or not: masturbate and edge regularly, highly recommended, but absolutely don't ejaculate

Masturbating and edging without ejaculating takes practice and willpower, especially if you've always ejaculated since you were a kid, and one amazing benefit is just that: not letting yourself quite reach that point builds willpower

In a relationship, the tremendous power is in controlling ejaculation with your partner too. You can absolutely reach 10 and have an amazing, longer-lasting orgasm without ejaculating, and end with incredible energy and power, way above baseline instead of back at square one. The more you do it, the more it builds. It takes practice for sure, and intention

Two big things help you gain control, in edging without ejaculating and in reaching 10 with incredible, powerful orgasms without ejaculating, with a partner or alone: breathing, and Kegels and reverse Kegels, which exercise your sex muscles and, with the right breathing techniques, let you start to control your arousal level

Most of us, most of our lives, have a habit a lot of people seem to get into as kids: arousal goes from like four to 10 on a linear, fast scale, you ejaculate and that's it, alone or with a woman. The fundamental shift is spending time in five, six, seven, eight, nine, going kind of up and down

Especially with a partner: get to eight or nine, bring it back down to five or six, let it rise and bring it down again, and your performance goes up powerfully, in how long you last and the pleasure you create for your partner
Alone, the pleasure is so much more in that range than skyrocketing to 10, and boom, you're drained and done
Partner or not, single or divorced, no ejaculating alone and no porn always apply: ejaculating alone and porn seem to be just fundamental things that suck the life out of you

You won't be perfect: you might slip over the edge unintentionally. Don't feel guilty or bummed, it happens: be intentional and get back on the practice. The difference you'll feel on a fundamental level is tremendous
With a woman and regular sex, the goal still seems to be separating orgasm and ejaculation, which takes practice
What to practice to move towards separating orgasm and ejaculation and gain control
To move towards separating orgasm and ejaculation and gain control, practice Kegels and reverse Kegels, to strengthen those muscles, and deep breathing

To move towards separating orgasm and ejaculation and gain control, practice meditation, which might sound unrelated but is incredibly related. Moving through five to nine on the arousal scale without going over the edge to 10, where your sex energy crashes, is so linked to your mind: it's not just physical. Controlling your breathing and harnessing your thoughts make a huge difference

Edging on a daily basis, alone, without ejaculating. If you're not used to it, you might need to start really easy and short, staying on the lower end of the scale. Feel what it's like to control and guide your sexual energy instead of an out-of-control 0 to 10 thing: a fundamental and powerful shift

Kegels and reverse Kegels are hugely important for controlling your sex energy. There seems to be no way to harness your maximum sexual power, and definitely no way to separate orgasm and ejaculation, without practicing Kegels. Like any muscle, your sex muscles, pretty important ones, are weak and waste away unexercised, and beyond sex or masturbating, Kegels and reverse Kegels exercise them intentionally

One app personally really liked to use, really good and worth trying: Stamena (S-T-A-M-E-N-A), with progressively more challenging timed routines of both Kegels and reverse Kegels. Pretty sure there's no affiliation. Personally, the iOS version, and pretty sure there's an Android one. Other apps exist, and of course you don't need one
To feel them: stop the flow mid-pee, and the muscles doing it are a Kegel. Trying to pee harder is a reverse Kegel
Done intentionally, they also build sex energy all on their own: if you're not doing Kegels now, you'll feel amazing boosts in your sort of internal fire

Do both. A lot of people just get into the habit of doing Kegels, if they do anything, and practicing just Kegels can make arousal harder to control: the Kegel side generally increases arousal, and you'll likely find squeezing takes you up the scale. You'll need that strength to eventually separate orgasm and ejaculation, but reverse Kegels are really important for controlling arousal

The key ones are three fundamental shifts: both Kegels and reverse Kegels, no jerking off to the point of ejaculation, no porn. Then you practice edging more and more, get better at controlling arousal, practice Kegels and reverse Kegels and get stronger, and after some practice you can reach a full-on, super powerful level 10 orgasm without ejaculating. Not in three days: more important is shifting how you look at it and when you allow yourself to ejaculate, which has a huge impact
Balance between the parts of life is really critical, and it matters in your body specifically too

Over the years, one finding has been kind of counterintuitive but almost universally true: when something starts hurting, it's almost never that thing that's the actual root cause. **Story:** thankfully no serious injuries, just little things here and there, some taking a few weeks to recover from
When your low back hurts, so often it's not your back at all that's weak or tight, but usually your glutes and hamstrings: tight, they pull on your low back
So often you feel the pain but aren't conscious of the tightness: unless you're closely paying attention, it's easy to miss that the area next to it, or balancing it, is kind of the root cause
Things that can make your low back hurt: standing or being on your feet a really long time, and things that really engage your glutes and hamstrings, especially if you're not used to it

Often, sitting too much tightens the front of the hips, the psoas muscles, throwing your body kind of out of balance front to back and causing back pain often enough. When the psoas, a really deep abdominal muscle, is tight, people probably extremely rarely feel pain there: what hurts is what it throws out of balance

**Story:** climbing almost daily, a lot at the gym, worked the upper-body pull muscles a lot while the push muscles didn't carry their weight, which overstressed the pull muscles and made them sore. Adding push-ups consistently, now alternated with climbing on a lot of solo days, made the climbing better, harder, longer and less painful, with a stronger feeling, because of the balance. Not surprising: too much pulling makes push muscles weak comparatively

Consider balance in your life, too: between individual, family and work time, leisure and activities. Getting out of balance causes issues: working nonstop maybe with your spouse or kids, playing nonstop maybe with your work

Balance between life's parts seems a little more obvious, maybe because we hear and think about it more, though a reminder still helps. Balance within the body, which affects us a lot, we really don't seem to hear a lot about

The encouragement: when something is tweaked, sore or hurting, consider that it may be a balance thing, the opposite or connected muscle, maybe the next muscles in the chain. With your back, it's not a front-to-back thing: a lot of times it's above or below in the chain, usually below, like your glutes and hamstrings, and even your calves and feet, causing low back pain through tightness in that chain

You can try this: different rollers work well, but some kind of massage roller works great (personally, a lot of different ones get used). Rolling out your body reveals tight spots you weren't conscious of, and it's like, "whoa. That's really tight"
Think about connected things and the opposite side, balance-wise: push versus pull, front versus back, left versus right. So often the root cause is not the one you think

**Story:** realizing this helped with pain and soreness: overall health and wellness got tremendously better, feeling strong without tight, sore, painful areas, as it helped figure out what was going on and deal with it more long term

**Story:** once a 7-Eleven-hot-dog-for-breakfast guy who didn't exercise, absolutely miserable, eating complete toxic nonsense, then a journey from about as low as you can get physically, mentally and emotionally, at least as it felt, to the strongest and best ever, at almost 40

Of the many ways to fuel your body, intermittent fasting, discovered just a few years ago, personally transformed health and fitness more than any other, and seems to have made the very most impact on life, body and mind too. **Story:** it came after years of trial and error with so many things nutritionally, first to lose fat and look a little better while overweight, then to feel better, be in shape and be strong

**Story:** for years of training, in pretty decent shape, ideas from various sources meant eating all the time, every two hours or whatever, and reaching 11 or 12 or one o'clock unfed brought almost a guilty feeling: "oh man, I should have eaten". Then, as it was kind of just working, without real hunger, came rolling with it, and the eating period kept shrinking. Intermittent fasting, less known then, was personally not even heard of, nor were its benefits known: it just worked, which led to investigating why
As it turns out, fasting has amazing benefits, even for just hours a day, giving your body a break from digesting food
Your testosterone immediately goes down when you eat, so intermittent fasting is incredibly powerful for supporting and boosting your hormones
Digestion is really the biggest energy draw on your body: it takes tremendous energy. **Story:** energy went up tremendously once fasting was part of the daily routine

Personally, the benefits are really wide and varied: more energy, a simpler life with fewer meals, putting on muscle and keeping off fat easier: everything about a shorter eating window has been incredibly beneficial

If there's one thing nutritionally to try, it's intermittent fasting. There's so much science now, but the bottom line: "Intermittent fasting just works", and it will probably, honestly, benefit your life

Ease into it gradually, so your body adapts. **Story:** eating now typically happens in about a two- to four-hour period each day, a fast of 20 to 22 hours. That's not a suggestion to jump at once from eating from breakfast until evening to only two or four hours

Eating from soon after waking until later, you're really not fasting except while you sleep. The best start is cutting out breakfast: you're already fasting from the evening, so start eating at noonish, with lunch, for at least a few hours in a true fasting state

It takes about 12 hours for your body to kind of shift gears into certain really beneficial processes. Stop eating at 7 p.m. and eat breakfast at 7 or 8 a.m., and you start eating just as those amazing benefits would begin. Skipping breakfast gives you at least a few hours a day past that point, enough to start feeling the benefits

A promise: you'll adapt quicker, and probably more easily, than you think. For a lot of people used to eating basically all their waking hours, fasting can seem kind of rough, but your body will adapt

The next step is your eating window: from when you start eating until you stop for the day. Breakfast by 8 a.m. and eating until 8 p.m., hopefully not later, is a 12-hour window. Cut it back more and more for more benefit: in personal experience, the shorter the window, the better the results
If there's one other thing to avoid food-wise, it's eating really late at night: it hurts your hormones and kills your morning wood
One caveat: still pay attention to what you fuel with during your window, especially as you cut it shorter, if you go that way: eat effectively, the right mix to support your activity and body
Training really hard, you sometimes have to really pay attention to eating enough
Not training super hard and maybe trying to keep extra weight off, it can still mean watching that you maybe don't eat too much, or some of the junkier things
The eating window is amazingly powerful, but not a complete magic bullet: four hours a day of fast food, and you're screwed. The fundamentals of eating good fuel still apply

Intermittent fasting is so powerful for how you feel, burning fat, keeping your metabolism up, your energy levels and building muscle really easily, and it works especially well for men, though it does work well for women also

If you haven't tried it, it very potentially could change your life from a nutritional fuel standpoint, so working towards it is highly encouraged: skip breakfast every day for a week and see how you feel and how long you take to adapt. Then, over time, in general, the shorter and earlier in the day your eating window, the better you'll feel
